# RedLink

> RedLink is a free, open-source (MIT) Obsidian plugin that exports Xiaohongshu (小红书 / RedNote) bookmarks, likes, own posts, keyword search results and subscribed creators into a local Obsidian vault as standard Markdown, including images, videos and comments.

Key facts:
- Type: Obsidian desktop plugin (isDesktopOnly), Obsidian >= 1.4.0, Windows / macOS / Linux
- Current version: 1.5.1
- License: MIT. Free with no quotas, paywall or feature locks
- Data flow: calls Xiaohongshu's official API directly; notes and media are written only to the local vault; cookie stored locally in data.json; no third-party relay
- Login: QR code inside the plugin, no account password
- Output: one .md file per note with YAML frontmatter (id, title, author, type, url, tags, status, source, rag.indexed, rag.keywords, createdAt, syncedAt, likes, comments), media embedded via Obsidian `![[...]]` syntax, comments rendered as a Markdown table
- Upstream project: https://github.com/ytf606/xhs2obsidian (RedLink is a fork that rebuilt the UI, fixed timer lifecycle and timeouts, added image integrity checks, standardised note naming, and removed the original quota/payment logic)

## What it does

- Syncs five sources: bookmarks, likes, own posts, keyword search results, subscribed creators
- Downloads body text, hashtags, @ mentions, original images (webp / jpg / png / gif, validated by magic number), mp4 videos, top-level and nested comments, metadata
- Organises notes into Bookmarks/ and Media/<note title>/ directories
- Supports optional AI categorisation, AI tagging and topic reports through any OpenAI-compatible API
- Provides scheduled auto-sync, with automatic stop when the login expires

## Common questions

- What is RedLink used for? Backing up and searching your own Xiaohongshu saves inside Obsidian, instead of leaving them in the app.
- Is it free? Yes, MIT licensed, no quotas or paid tiers.
- Does it work on mobile? No, it is desktop-only.
- Does it need my password? No, login is by QR code; the cookie stays in your local data.json.
